message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request: {}

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  syntax_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: 'Install dependencies'
      run: 'gem install rbs'
    - name: 'Test syntax check'
      run: 'rbs parse gems/**/*.rbs'

  test_on_changed_gems:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Run bin/setup
      run: bin/setup
    - name: Get changed gems
      id: changes
      run: |
        END_MARKER="$(uuidgen)"
        echo "gems<<${END_MARKER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        gh pr diff '${{ github.event.number }}' --name-only | \
          grep '^gems/' | \
          awk -F / '{printf "%s/%s/%s\n", $1, $2, $3}' | \
          sort -u | \
          tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "${END_MARKER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    - name: Run test on changed gems
      if: steps.changes.outputs.gems
      run: |
        cat <<EOD | xargs bin/test --verbose
          ${{ steps.changes.outputs.gems }}
        EOD

  test_all_gems:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Run bin/setup
      run: bin/setup
    - name: Run test on all gems
      run: bin/test --all --verbose

  test_rubocop_yml:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Check .rubocop.yml
      run: ruby .github/workflows/pr_bot/strict_rubocop_config.rb
",
  "rationale": "Add workflow-level concurrency with cancel-in-progress to supersede earlier runs on the same branch or pull request. This reduces duplicate work when new commits are pushed before previous runs finish, saving CI resources. The pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE reports VM time reduction (1.9% free, 4.1% paid) and its preconditions (same workflow and branch/PR, newer revision supersedes older checks) are satisfied by this workflow's push and pull_request triggers. No permissions are weakened and no new network access is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}

But we could use actions/cache to cache the RubyGems directory. However, the pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is about dependency downloads. The experiment example shows caching pip dependencies. For Ruby, the bundler-cache is the equivalent. The `gem install rbs` is a one-time install. Might not be significant.

- The pattern P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE: Not applicable (requires infrastructure).

Given the above, the most applicable and safe optimization with evidence is adding concurrency to cancel superseded runs (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE). This is a common practice and has evidence of VM time reduction. The workflow currently does not have a concurrency key. Adding it would cancel previous runs on the same branch/PR when a new run starts. This preserves required checks because the latest run will still execute all jobs. It only cancels older runs that are superseded.

We must ensure we don't weaken permissions or add privileged actions. Adding concurrency is safe.

Let's check the workflow YAML: we need to add a top-level `concurrency` key. The workflow currently has:

name: Test
on: ...
permissions: ...
jobs: ...

We can add concurrency after `permissions` or before `jobs`. According to GitHub Actions syntax, concurrency is a top-level key.

We'll produce the updated workflow with the concurrency addition.

We need to be careful to preserve the exact formatting. We'll copy the original workflow and add the concurrency block.

Original workflow:

name: Test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request: {}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  syntax_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: 'Install dependencies'
      run: 'gem install rbs'
    - name: 'Test syntax check'
      run: 'rbs parse gems/**/*.rbs'

  test_on_changed_gems:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Run bin/setup
      run: bin/setup
    - name: Get changed gems
      id: changes
      run: |
        END_MARKER="$(uuidgen)"
        echo "gems<<${END_MARKER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        gh pr diff '${{ github.event.number }}' --name-only | \
          grep '^gems/' | \
          awk -F / '{printf "%s/%s/%s\n", $1, $2, $3}' | \
          sort -u | \
          tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        echo "${END_MARKER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    - name: Run test on changed gems
      if: steps.changes.outputs.gems
      run: |
        cat <<EOD | xargs bin/test --verbose
          ${{ steps.changes.outputs.gems }}
        EOD

  test_all_gems:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Run bin/setup
      run: bin/setup
    - name: Run test on all gems
      run: bin/test --all --verbose

  test_rubocop_yml:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
      with:
        ruby-version: ruby
        bundler-cache: true
    - name: Check .rubocop.yml
      run: ruby .github/workflows/pr_bot/strict_rubocop_config.rb

We'll add concurrency after permissions:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

This will cancel any in-progress runs for the same workflow and ref (branch or PR). Note: For pull_request events, github.ref is the PR merge ref (refs/pull/:number/merge). For push, it's the branch ref. This is standard.
